I'm not entirely convinced AMD has the right idea here. The 15 Watt TDP puts it on par with Intel's solutions, and no doubt AMD's onboard GPU will significantly outperform Intel's - however Intel is most likely still going to provide better CPU performance. So who's really the target audience then? For "light" users Intel's faster CPU will mean more then AMD's better GPU, for gamers AMD's GPU while better still isn't good enough so your back to a CPU + discrete GPU where again Intel's CPU looks better. I really want AMD to succeed but I just don't see how can happen unless AMD significantly improves their IPC.
What happened to AMD? Back when they bought ATI i thought they'd roll over Intel completely.

Bulldozer happened. AMD brought 64-bit computing to the desktop and was producing a superior product compared to Intel thanks in part to Intel's own disaster microarchitecture, Netburst. Bulldozer underperformed at a time right when Intel had just successfully dug themselves out their Netburst hole, and AMD had no real follow up to make them competitive with Intel again.
AMD also lost a lot of money trying to build their own fabrication facility, Global Foundries. Because this is part of Intel's dominance.
